thread.title: Stocks Mixed In Week; SEC Sues Tesla CEO Elon Musk; Fed Hikes Rates; Nike Earnings Top; Pot Stocks Buzzing | Investor's Business Daily

author: IBD STAFF
title: Stocks Mixed In Week; SEC Sues Tesla CEO Elon Musk; Fed Hikes Rates; Nike Earnings Top; Pot Stocks Buzzing | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones and S&P 500 index fell last week, with the Nasdaq composite rising somewhat. Tesla stock plunged Friday after the SEC sued CEO Elon Musk over his Tesla ( TSLA ) go-private tweets. Nike ( NKE ) earnings were strong, and marijuana stocks were buzzing amid new deals and products. Crude oil prices hit new highs as OPEC shrugged at President Donald Trump's demands for more supply. The Fed hiked rates and signaled that more are on the way, while chief Jerome Powell said "some asset prices" are high.
X Dow Jones Falls; Nasdaq Rises The Nasdaq composite rose modestly for the week but fell slightly in September. The Dow Jones and S&P 500 index pulled back but advanced for the month. Energy stocks, Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) were among the weekly winners, along with some software, apparel and medical-product names.
SEC Sues Tesla CEO Elon Musk The SEC sued Tesla CEO Elon Musk, accusing him of securities fraud for "a series of false and misleading tweets" in August. Musk tweeted Aug. 7 that he might take the electric automaker private at $420 per share, claiming "funding secured." Tesla stock tumbled 14% Friday. The SEC seeks to bar Musk from leading Tesla or any other public company. Analysts warned of dire consequences, in terms of demand for cars, employee morale and the ability to raise capital. A Musk exit could cost Tesla stock big since shares have "about $130 of Musk premium for future success," Barclays said.
Fed Will Keep Raising Rates; Powell Warns On Asset Prices The Fed hiked its key interest rate by a quarter point on Wednesday while indicating another hike is to come in December and three more next year. Fed policymaker projections suggest little concern about an outbreak of inflation. But members still expect to push interest rates past neutral to keep the economy from financial excesses. Fed Chairman Jerome Powell said that financial stability risks to the economy are moderate, noting that "some asset prices are in the upper reach of their historic ranges."
Nike Earnings Top, Sales Guidance So-So Nike topped Q1 2019 estimates, with EPS up 17.5% to 67 cents and sales up 10% to $9.95 billion, but it sees revenue growth at the lower end of the previously provided range. North America sales rose 6% — twice Q4 growth and continuing a turnaround for the region. Nike said full-price product sales were "significantly outpacing" off-price sales on the strength of new products. Its revamped retail strategy that focuses on elevating Nike's brand in athletic apparel stores has resulted in "relatively strong growth," said management. Shares initially tumbled Wednesday but pared losses and closed the week down 1%, and still in buy range.
Pot Stocks Less Volatile, Make Deals Canopy Growth ( CGC ) shareholders OK'd the planned $4 billion investment by Corona parent Constellation Brands ( STZ ) in the marijuana producer. The move will clear the way for two Constellation executives to become Canopy directors. Tilray ( TLRY ) will buy medical marijuana from Supreme Cannabis in a supply deal, and it said it had successfully exported medical cannabis to Australia to treat children with intractable epilepsy. Shares rallied after spiking and crashing last week. Canadian marijuana company Aurora Cannabis confirmed that it planned to list on a big U.S. exchange. India Globalization Capital ( IGC ) vaulted as it entered the CBD-drinks market.
GW Pharmaceuticals ( GWPH ) jumped 7% Thursday as the DEA listed its cannabis-based epilepsy drug Epidiolex as Schedule 5, the lowest restriction. That clears the final hurdle for Epidiolex to be sold in the U.S.
Medical Device Stocks Pumped Medical-device stocks Boston Scientific ( BSX ), Edwards Lifesciences ( EW ) and Abiomed ( ABMD ) joined the IBD 50 in the latest week amid a flurry of news stemming from the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics meeting in San Diego. During that meeting, Abbott Laboratories ( ABT ) announced its MitraClip works in group of hard-to-treat patients with leaky heart valves. Boston said its drug-eluting stent, Eluvia, beat out a rival in a head-to-head test. Afterward, Eluvia gained FDA approval. Meanwhile, Edwards broke out Monday. It has a product related to Abbott's MitraClip. Also, Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) was rumored to be interested in buying Edwards or Boston Sci.
Crude Oil Hits Multiyear Highs Brent crude rose 5% to $82.73 a barrel, hitting multiyear highs, after OPEC signaled no plans to increase production any time soon, even as President Trump thundered in his U.N. speech that the cartel is "ripping off the rest of the world." U.S. crude stockpiles unexpectedly rose by 1.9 million barrels last week, the first increase in six weeks, according to the Energy Information Administration. Domestic production rose to 11.1 million barrels per day, up from 11 million bpd in the prior week. U.S. crude futures rose 3.5% to $73.25 a barrel.
Facebook: 50 Million Users At Risk Facebook ( FB ) said Friday that attackers exploited a vulnerability, affecting some 50 million users exposed. Facebook reset 90 million passwords as a precaution. Earlier in the week, Instagram co-founders Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger are leaving the photo-sharing app, which acquired in 2012. Several reports cited their discontent with Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg taking more day-to-day control of Instagram.
Michael Kors Will Buy Versace The American affordable luxury apparel and handbag giant agreed to buy iconic Italian fashion house Versace for $2.1 billion and is looking to add more upscale brands to its offerings. Michael Kors ( KORS ) expects to eventually more than double Versace sales to $2 billion a year and expand the number of stores to 300 from 200. The new combined company will be called Capri Holdings. Kors stock tumbled 5.7%
Two other well-known U.S. companies are changing their names. Weight Watchers ( WTW ) is now WW. Dunkin' Brands ( DNKN ) is renaming its Dunkin' Donuts unit as just Dunkin' starting Jan. 1.
Tech Giants Testify On Data Privacy At a Senate Commerce Committee hearing, executives from Apple ( AAPL ), AT&T ( T ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOGL ) and Twitter ( TWTR ) urged Congress to develop national protections that would supplant state-level regulations. The executives expressed broad support for a national consumer privacy law but offered few specifics. The tech leaders seemed to agree on broad privacy principles, such as giving users more transparency about how their data is being used. Google CEO Sundar Pichai met with GOP lawmakers privately Friday.
SurveyMonkey Pops In IPO Debut The most closely watched IPO was SurveyMonkey ( SVMK ), a provider of online services for conducting surveys. Shares in the upsized IPO priced at 12, above the high end of the range. The IPO raised $180 million. Shares popped 44% on the first day of trading. September was one of the busiest months for IPO activity this year. But they were relatively small.
News In Brief Accenture ( ACN ) earnings rose 7% to $1.58 a share, with revenue rising 11% vs. a year earlier to $10.1 billion, both narrowly topping expectations. But the IT services giant forecast fiscal 2019 profit below analyst estimates. Shares fell modestly but stayed in buy range.
Square ( SQ ) stock popped to an all-time high after one analyst hiked his price target on the digital payments processor — on views that it will disrupt markets in a way similar to FANG stocks. Square also announced a new mobile business app, hitting shares in Paychex ( PAYX ) and Ceridian HCM ( CDAY ).
Comcast ( CMCSA ) will buy 21st Century Fox Entertainment's 39% stake in Sky, gaining full control of the British satellite TV broadcaster. Walt Disney ( DIS ), which has agreed to buy Fox ( FOXA ), will receive just over $15 billion for the Sky stake. Comcast outbid Fox for control of Sky in a showdown auction.
Cruise-ship operator Carnival ( CCL ) on Thursday reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter earnings but gave weak EPS guidance for the current quarter. Shares fell sharply Thursday. Royal Caribbean ( RCL ) initially fell but slashed losses to stay in buy range.
BMW ( BMWYY ) became the latest automaker to cut its profit forecast, sending its stock sharply lower. It cited pricing pressure, trade conflicts and tougher emission tests in the European Union.
Sirius XM Holdings ( SIRI ) agreed to buy Pandora Media ( P ), creating the world's largest audio entertainment company. The all-stock transaction was worth $3.5 billion when it was announced Sept. 24.
CarMax ( KMX ) earnings jumped 27% to $1.24 a share, topping estimates. The big used-car dealer's revenue also beat, growing 9% to $4.77 billion. But average selling-price growth cooled. CarMax stock reversed lower Wednesday.
Barrick Gold ( ABX ) jumped after the world's largest gold miner agreed to buy British rival Randgold Resources ( GOLD ) in a deal valued at $6 billion.
Sonic ( SONC ) will be taken private in a buyout by Inspire Brands, the parent of Arby's, in a $2.3 billion deal including debt. Inspire will pay $43.50 per share in cash for the drive-in chain. The Sonic deal is the latest in several recent restaurant takeovers, including Inspire's takeover of Buffalo Wild Wings and privately held Cava's purchase of fast-casual Mediterranean chain Zoe's Kitchen ( ZOES ).
